title: Luna and the Shooting Star Night | Asking for Help Is Smart
lesson: Asking for help is not a weakness. Even the smartest friend has only two wings, and things go better together.
description: Luna promised to show all her friends a shooting star, but she has a secret: she has read forty books about stars and never used a telescope! Will she keep pretending, or be brave enough to ask for help? A funny starry adventure about asking for help and teamwork.

lines.text: CRASH! Somewhere under a giant pile of books, maps and one very shiny telescope... was Luna.
I'm fine! Everything is under control! Mostly! Can someone find my left wing?
Luna! Whoa. Are you building a fort out of books?
No! Tonight is the Star Shower. I promised everyone I would show them a shooting star.
I have forty books about stars. I am the star expert of Maple Hollow. I can do it all by myself!
Cool! Can I help carry something? Anything? This book is bigger than me.
No thank you! Experts don't need help. Probably. I read that somewhere. I think.
In the meadow, Luna tried her new telescope for the very first time. A telescope makes faraway things look close.
Easy. I just look in here and... Bolt! Why are you so tiny? And so far away?
I am not far away. I am right here. Distance to Luna: one wing.
Luna, you're looking in the wrong end! Ha! Even I know that. And I've never read a book about telescopes.
I knew that. I was... testing the wrong end. For science.
Do you want help? I have a plan. Plan one: I read the instructions out loud. Very loud.
And I can carry everything up Lookout Hill! I bet I can do it in ten seconds. On three!
No, no! I've got it. Really. You two just come tonight and be amazed.
Chance that Luna has got it: forty-one percent. And falling.
At sunset, Luna started up the forest path. She carried the telescope, the tent, the lantern, and nine books.
Wobble. Wobble. Whoa! Okay. Step one says: attach part A to part A-and-a-half. What is part A-and-a-half?
Well, hello, Luna! I'm walking to the hill too. I started after lunch. Nearly there!
Grandpa, can I tell you a secret? I've read forty books about stars. But I've never actually used a telescope.
If I ask for help, everyone will think I'm not smart.
Ha! A hundred years ago, I carried a giant watermelon up this hill. All by myself. It took me three days.
At the top, my friend was waiting with a wheelbarrow. He said, I had it the whole time! You never asked!
Three days? For one watermelon?
And it was a little squashed by then. Remember, Luna. Even the smartest owl has only two wings.
At the top of Lookout Hill, the friends were waiting. Luna took a deep breath.
Everyone? I need to tell you something. I don't know how to set up the telescope. Can you please help me?
Of course! I've been waiting all day for you to ask!
Asking for help detected. New skill unlocked. Beep boop!
Okay, team! I'll set up the tent. Milo, hold the legs. Bolt, read the steps. On three!
STEP ONE! ATTACH PART A TO PART A-AND-A-HALF!
Bolt, you don't have to read it that loud. Oh! Wait! Part A-and-a-half is this little screw!
Click. Twist. Click. Four friends finished in four minutes. Luna alone had needed forty.
We did it! And I didn't drop a single book. Well, only two.
Night came. Grandpa Shell had arrived too, of course. Star watching is a friends-and-grown-ups job.
My turn! I see... one star. Just one star. It's not moving at all.
WHOOSH! There goes one! Over there! And another one! Behind you, Milo!
What? Where? I missed it! The telescope only shows a tiny piece of sky!
Hmm. When I was young, I watched a shooting star night through a pipe. Saw nothing. Very nice pipe, though.
That's it! I read about this! Shooting stars fly across the whole sky. The best way to see them is with just your eyes!
And they aren't really stars. They're tiny bits of space dust, some as small as sand, burning up high in the air.
So we carried a telescope up a hill... to not use it?
We can use it for the Moon! But first, everyone lie down and look up!
WHOOSH. WHOOSH. Shooting stars zipped across the sky, one after another.
Thank you, everyone. I couldn't do this alone. Asking for help was scary. But it was the smartest thing I did all day.
And nobody had to carry a watermelon for three days.
I counted forty-eight shooting stars! How many did you count, Bolt?
Forty-seven. Pepper wins. Plan two: I ask Pepper for help counting next time.
Yes! I win! Wait... was that a race?
With you, Pepper, everything is a race!
Asking for help doesn't make you less smart. It lets your friends shine too. See you next time in Maple Hollow!
